findings.title: Every internally authorized policy-window request loses the field required at first claim
findings.evidence: Line 206 derives an authorized finite policy window and persists an internal grant with policyWindowId. Line 207 copies grantId/maxParentTokens/sourceRunId/sourceResultHash/historyAcknowledgedUnknown into request.continuationGrant, but omits grant.policyWindowId. The same request.supervisor does include that ID. Line 168 requires continuationGrant.policyWindowId === supervisor.policyWindowId and validates the bound window. The comparison is therefore undefined versus the actual hash for every such request. claim():235 and the local pump both use that preflight.
findings.impact: The first genuine unknown-history, over-cumulative-token or listed-terminal-boundary continuation that reaches this policy path is queued but cannot be claimed. The claimed continuous original-goal path is not operational at its critical boundary.
findings.narrowFix: Carry the already validated policyWindowId into request.continuationGrant, through the formal request and claim representation, retaining exact source, current generation and bound-window validation. The formal ExecutionRequest continuationGrant schema already allows this field; do not remove preflight's policy equality or revocation checks.
findings.whySavedTestsMissIt: execution-createapp-chain.test.ts:26,34 uses a 1000-token template and three 5-token child results, never requiring a boundary grant. supervisor-policy-context.test.ts:2 replaces supervisorDispatch with a stub that directly authorizes/binds a window, bypassing the real request construction and preflight.

findings.title: An exact replay cannot recover a policy grant committed before the business request
findings.evidence: The policy path calls grantContinuation, whose separate transaction commits the grant at line 187 before the repository request transaction at line 209. If the process exits or the business request fails after grant persistence but before request commit, the next exact durable dispatch intent still has no matching runtime/business request at lines 196/198. The same policy source/decision/context yields the same window ID (supervisor-goal-policy.ts:14), but line 206 rejects any existing grant command_id for that window, including the exact pending unconsumed grant. grantContinuation's existing idempotent replay at lines 180-181 is never reached.
findings.impact: A recoverable persistence cut permanently blocks the authorized window instead of reconstructing the same request. It does not cause duplicate execution, but it breaks restart/replay continuation under the original authority.
findings.narrowFix: Recover and validate the exact matching pending grant/window for the deterministic request, reusing its original ID after checking request hash, owner/task CAS, source/result hash, policy generation and consumption binding. Reject genuinely different or already bound requests. Complete the existing cross-store recovery path without minting another window or blindly retrying a child/model.
findings.importantCorrectionToInitialMessage: Lines 196 and 198 do explicitly call bindWindow while recovering an already committed runtime/business request. An initial truncated-read suspicion that those branches lacked bindWindow was withdrawn and is not a finding. The confirmed cut here is specifically grant committed while no business request exists.

findings.title: Real awaiting-cost task state is rejected before its authorized successor can use a window
findings.evidence: result():317 maps a real signed outcome awaiting-cost to task.status=waitingUser and executionStatus=awaiting-cost. R7 supervisor runtime:59,73 now accepts and analyzes that signed source and can produce continue. But supervisorDispatch():200 permits a consumed task only when its status is validating/failed/blocked/paused/cancelled, excluding waitingUser. It fails SUPERVISOR_SOURCE_INVALID before reaching the awaiting-cost policy/grant branch at line 206.
findings.impact: The R6 admission-to-judgment problem is partly repaired, but the real cost-unknown source still cannot reach an authorized successor through ExecutionRuntime. Helper tests with a stub executor cannot prove this path works.
findings.narrowFix: Align the consumed-task state admission with the already verified awaiting-cost signed source, source hash, task CAS and current goal/window authorization. Permit only the specific trustworthy cost-boundary case, rather than broadly authorizing every waitingUser task. Keep unknown cost/history and original failure evidence; do not relabel the source success or fill zero usage.
findings.whySavedTestsMissIt: supervisor-reconcile-r43.test.ts:2 seeds waitingUser/awaiting-cost but provides a stub supervisorDispatch and only asserts no dispatch after a failed model. supervisor-policy-context.test.ts:2 likewise uses a stub executor, so neither invokes ExecutionRuntime line 200.

policyCoverageAndLimits.item: Known over-limit and unknown-history finite windows
policyCoverageAndLimits.assessment: Unknown remains explicitly acknowledged in policy/grant rather than zero; finite maxParentTokens<=10M, timeout<=1200, one round/zero retry and record-only money remain bounded. R7-A-P1-01 and 03 prevent the real supported successor paths. Saved helper tests do not hit production dispatch/preflight.

Pause/stop/takeover/revise/current correction revoke policy generation; dispatch and claim call current supervisor/window validation. supervisor-policy-context.test.ts asserts validateWindow becomes false after pause, but its claim step is a stub assertion, not actual ExecutionRuntime.claim. The claimed zero-new-execution full chain remains unverified.

Helper policy DB close/reopen preserves a bound window and rejects different directives/run binding. ExecutionRuntime recovers existing runtime/business requests and rebinds their window at 196/198. The pre-business pending-grant cut remains blocked as R7-A-P1-02. No real multi-store ExecutionRuntime/journal restart matrix is saved.

At >=20, a current active policy permits further finite windows without another owner grant; there is no distinct recorded 20-round objective-progress checkpoint in this source. Identical continue directive and three consecutive non-success outcomes cause STALLED. These are technical heuristics, not proof of objective progress, achieved criteria or actual stop. No saved 20-round/stalled full chain was supplied; this is an implementation/verification limit rather than an additional asserted P1.
